arxiv-1901-06285.title: Game-Theoretic Randomness for Blockchain Games
arxiv-1901-06285.creator: Daniel Kraft
arxiv-1901-06285.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Daniel Kraft. In this paper, we consider the problem of generating fair randomness in a deterministic, multi-agent context (for instance, a decentralised game built on a blockchain). The existing state-of-the-art approaches are either susceptible to manipulation if the stakes are high enough, or they are not generally applicable (specifically for massive game worlds as opposed to games between a small set of players).

arxiv-2005-06133.title: Adaptive Rule Discovery for Labeling Text Data
arxiv-2005-06133.creator: Sainyam Galhotra Behzad Golshan Wang-Chiew Tan
arxiv-2005-06133.description: Abstract Creating and collecting labeled data is one of the major bottlenecks in machine learning pipelines and the emergence of automated feature generation techniques such as deep learning, which typically requires a lot of training data, has further exacerbated the problem.

arxiv-2205-06922.title: Exploring How Machine Learning Practitioners (Try To) Use Fairness Toolkits Conference: 2022 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency; June 21–24, 2022; Seoul, Republic of Korea 2022 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (FAccT ’22), June 21–24, 2022, Seoul
arxiv-2205-06922.creator: Wesley Hanwen Deng, Manish Nagireddy, Michelle Seng Ah Lee, Jatinder Singh, Zhiwei Steven Wu, Kenneth Holstein, Haiyi Zhu
arxiv-2205-06922.description: Abstract . Recent years have seen the development of many open-source ML fairness toolkits aimed at helping ML practitioners assess and address unfairness in their systems. However, there has been little research investigating how ML practitioners actually use these toolkits in practice.

arxiv-2211-14328.title: Spectral response of disorder-free localized lattice gauge theories
arxiv-2211-14328.creator: Nilotpal Chakraborty, Markus Heyl, Petr Karpov, Roderich Moessner
arxiv-2211-14328.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Nilotpal Chakraborty, Markus Heyl, Petr Karpov, Roderich Moessner. We show that certain lattice gauge theories exhibiting disorder-free localization have a characteristic response in spatially averaged spectral functions: a few sharp peaks combined with vanishing response in the zero frequency limit. This reflects the discrete spectra of small clusters of kinetically active regions formed in such gauge theories when they fragment into spatially finite clusters in the localized phase due to the presence of static charges.

arxiv-2403-08487.title: Model Will Tell: Training Membership Inference for Diffusion Models
arxiv-2403-08487.creator: Xiaomeng Fu, Xi Wang, Qiao Li, Jin Liu, Jiao Dai, Jizhong Han
arxiv-2403-08487.description: Abstract Diffusion models pose risks of privacy breaches and copyright disputes, primarily stemming from the potential utilization of unauthorized data during the training phase. The Training Membership Inference (TMI) task aims to determine whether a specific sample has been used in the training process of a target model, representing a critical tool for privacy violation verification.

arxiv-2403-09620.title: PosSAM: Panoptic Open-vocabulary Segment Anything Thanks: Qualcomm AI Research, an initiative of Qualcomm Technologies, Inc.
arxiv-2403-09620.creator: Vibashan VS, Shubhankar Borse ∗, Hyojin Park, Debasmit Das, Vishal Patel, Munawar Hayat, Fatih Porikli
arxiv-2403-09620.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce an open-vocabulary panoptic segmentation model that effectively unifies the strengths of the Segment Anything Model (SAM) with the vision-language CLIP model in an end-to-end framework. While SAM excels in generating spatially-aware masks, it’s decoder falls short in recognizing object class information and tends to oversegment without additional guidance.

arxiv-2403-15636.title: On the Variational Interpretation of Mirror Play in Monotone Games
arxiv-2403-15636.creator: Yunian Pan, Tao Li, Quanyan Zhu
arxiv-2403-15636.description: Abstract Mirror play (MP) is a well-accepted primal-dual multi-agent learning algorithm where all agents simultaneously implement mirror descent in a distributed fashion. The advantage of MP over vanilla gradient play lies in its usage of mirror maps that better exploit the geometry of decision domains.

arxiv-2409-05459.title: Beyond Flatland: A Geometric Take on Matching Methods for Treatment Effect Estimation
arxiv-2409-05459.creator: Melanie F. Pradier, Javier González
arxiv-2409-05459.description: Abstract Matching is a popular approach in causal inference to estimate treatment effects by pairing treated and control units that are most similar in terms of their covariate information. However, classic matching methods completely ignore the geometry of the data manifold, which is crucial to define a meaningful distance for matching, and struggle when covariates are noisy and high-dimensional.

arxiv-2410-18316.title: Periodic orbits for square and rectangular billiards
arxiv-2410-18316.creator: Hongjia H. Chen, Hinke M. Osinga
arxiv-2410-18316.description: Abstract Mathematical billiards is much like the real game: a point mass, representing the ball, rolls in a straight line on a (perfectly friction-less) table, striking the sides according to the law of reflection. A billiard trajectory is then completely characterised by the number of elastic collisions.

arxiv-2507-16513.title: Graphical Analysis of Nonlinear Multivariable Feedback Systems
arxiv-2507-16513.creator: Julius P.J. Krebbekx, Roland Tóth, Amritam Das
arxiv-2507-16513.description: Abstract Scaled Relative Graphs (SRGs) provide a novel graphical frequency-domain method for the analysis of nonlinear systems. There have been recent efforts to generalize SRG analysis to Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems. However, these attempts yielded only results for square systems, and in some cases, only methods applicable for Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) systems.

pmc-11670242.title: Inferring phase transitions and critical exponents from limited observations with thermodynamic maps
pmc-11670242.creator: Lukas Herron, Kinjal Mondal, John S. Schneekloth, Pratyush Tiwary
pmc-11670242.description: SignificancePhase transitions play a pivotal role in diverse scientific domains, from metal solidification to water boiling and biological macromolecule folding. However, quantifying these transitions, especially their temperature-dependent attributes, presents challenges due to complex and sparse data. This study introduces “thermodynamic maps” (TM), an approach merging statistical mechanics, molecular simulations, and generative AI.

pmc-11689251.title: LEVERAGING PATIENT PORTALS TO IDENTIFY AND INTERVENE IN DEMENTIA CARE: CAREGIVING, MEDICATION, AND ACUTE CARE
pmc-11689251.creator: Jennifer Portz, George Demiris
pmc-11689251.description: Care partners play a pivotal role in supporting people living with dementia (PLWD), yet their systematic identification and involvement in clinical care are often lacking. This symposium presents four studies highlighting ground-breaking care partner identification methods to inform patient portal-based interventions targeting care partners to enhance dementia care.

pmc-12755346.title: AI in Psychiatric Education and Training From 2016 to 2024: Scoping Review of Trends
pmc-12755346.creator: Michael James Weightman, Anna Chur-Hansen, Scott Richard Clark
pmc-12755346.description: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly changing both clinical psychiatry and the education of medical professionals. However, little is currently known about how AI is being discussed in the education and training of psychiatry for medical students and doctors around the world.ObjectiveThis paper aims to provide a snapshot of the available data on this subject as of 2024.

pmc-13204838.title: LRG1 as a Potential Therapeutic Target in Atherosclerosis: Mechanistic Basis and Current Evidence
pmc-13204838.creator: Jianan Wu, Xia Yi, Lanlan Wang, Kaixuan Yang, Minghuan Liu, Jiawei Song, Zenghui Yue
pmc-13204838.description: Highlights What are the main findings? LRG1 is closely associated with inflammatory amplification, endothelial dysfunction, aberrant angiogenesis, and extracellular matrix remodeling in atherosclerosis.Current evidence from clinical studies, lesional observations, and experimental models supports LRG1 as a candidate molecule with potential relevance to plaque progression and structural evolution. What are the implications of the main findings?

pmc-13240269.title: Stability‐Driven Selection of EEG Connectivity Features for Psychosis Classification: A Network‐Based Machine Learning Approach
pmc-13240269.creator: Mahdi Naeim, Mohammad Narimani
pmc-13240269.description: ObjectivesTo develop a network‐based machine learning framework for classifying psychosis using EEG connectivity features and to identify stable, reproducible candidate markers through a stability‐driven approach.MethodsThis study was designed as a cross‐sectional analytical secondary data analysis using a publicly available EEG dataset comprising 43 participants (19 psychosis, 24 controls).

pmc-13263815.title: Platelet-rich plasma in selected urological conditions: a narrative review of biological rationale, current evidence, and limitations
pmc-13263815.creator: Long Huang, Zongshuai Gao, Xiang Ren, Zhufan Xu, Changtai Zhu
pmc-13263815.description: Background and ObjectivePlatelet-rich plasma (PRP) has been increasingly investigated as an autologous regenerative product in urology. Its proposed biological effects, including angiogenesis, inflammation modulation, neuroprotection, and tissue remodeling, have prompted exploratory use in erectile dysfunction (ED), Peyronie’s disease (PD), interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS), urethral reconstruction, and urinary incontinence.

pmc-13270288.title: Ageing of inverse vulcanised polymers
pmc-13270288.creator: Christian W. Schmitt, Andy Mach, Valeria Berner, Eric Pohl, Joseph J. Dale, Birgit Huber, Dominik Voll, Emmanuel Richaud, Ute Schepers, Carl-Christoph Höhne, Patrick Théato
pmc-13270288.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Inverse vulcanised polymers are an emerging class of materials with a broad range of applications from energy storage to fertiliser systems. As these materials are still subject of research, scaling to real-life applications is just underway. One major factor for these materials to be fit for industrial use is their ageing behaviour under environmental influences such as temperature, sunlight, moisture and pH or biological attack.
